newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil expands jetty at Kaarstoe terminal.
newsitem.headline: Statoil expands jetty at Kaarstoe terminal.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS is expanding one of the two jetties at the Kaarstoe terminal on the west coast of Norway to increase the size of vessels able to moor at the plant by almost 40 percent, a spokesman for Statoil said on Tuesday.
The expansion is part of preparations to handle increasing volumes of liquefied petroleum gases (LPG) and condensate as new fields on the Norwegian continental shelf are brought on stream.

Helge Hoel, Statoil spokesman at Kaarstoe, said the extension would permit vessels up to 275 metres in length to take delivery at the jetty against 210 metres today. Depth also be increase by one metre to 13 metres.
"This means we will be able to accept ships of up to 110,000 deadweight tonnes compared with 80,000 tonnes at the moment," Hoel said.

Hoel said LPG volumes were expected to rise rapidly once the Aasgard development off mid-Norway begins gas production in October 2000. No decision has been made by the Aasgard licence partners on where oil from the development will be landed.

The terminal, which delivered 3.1 million tonnes of condensate and 3.0 million tonnes of LPG in 1996, has a processing capacity of 7-7.5 million tonnes per year, he said. This will be expanded to around 10 million tonnes per year by 2000.
"By 2000 we expect around 600 ships to use the terminal per year, plus or minus 50 depending on their size," Hoel said. This compared with a total of 363 vessels in 1994 and 398 last year.
The expansion of the jetty should be completed in May.
